is pleased to announce that drilling has started on its Phase 2B Reverse Circulation (“RC”) drill program at the La Union Project in Sonora, Mexico, as outlined in the Company’s news release dated November 9, 2026. The drill rig has been mobilized and is now drilling at the Luis Hill target. At Luis Hill, this program will follow up on the sediment-hosted gold mineralization intersected in Phase 1 drilling. Step-out drilling will go deeper than previous holes to test the newly identified induced polarization (IP) geophysical target and the extent of the shale beds encountered during core drilling.

When drilling at Luis Hill is complete, the rig will move to the Union Mine. Riverside is the operator, and Questcorp Mining Inc. is the option partner (see news release dated May 6, 2025). Since that option agreement was announced, further target definition work has identified at least three mineralized mantos at the Union Mine. These will be tested along with the previously outlined feeder structure.
Phase 2B Program Highlights
Approximately 600 m of RC drilling is underway in two holes of approximately 300 m each.
Luis Hill: one hole testing the IP chargeability anomaly described in the Company’s November 9, 2026 news release (see Figures 2 & 3).
Union Mine: one hole testing the continuity of the feeder structure and at least three newly identified mineralized mantos near the historic workings (see Figure 4).
Drilling managed by Riverside as operator, with exploration funded by Questcorp under the option agreement.

“We are pleased to continue Phase 2 drilling using a new drilling method, which we believe can be faster and collect a larger volume of sample,” said John-Mark Staude, President and CEO of Riverside Resources. “We are excited to test the geophysical features that tie in with the geology and past mining. Completing the Phase 2 program will set us up for the next phase of drilling, and we look forward to further exploration work at the La Union Project.”

Luis Hill Target

The Phase 2B hole at Luis Hill is testing the IP chargeability anomaly, with a near-vertical hole to approximately 350 m depth (Figure 3). The hole is expected to test the mineralized horizon and nearby intrusions. Contacts between these intrusions and favourable host rocks may provide settings for mineralization.

Union Mine Target

The Union Mine structure is hosted in the Clemente Formation, a major carbonate replacement deposit ("CRD") host unit. This hole will test the continuity of the Union Mine feeder structure, where sampling returned 30 meters of chip channel sample with grades 20.2 g/t Au, 226 g/t Ag, and 2.7% Zn of continuous sampling (news release, January 22, 2026). The Union Mine structure appears to have a geophysical expression in the magnetic tilt product (Figure 4A). The hole will also test for three potentially mineralized stacked mantos projected southward from the main historical mineralized zone of the Union Mine (Figure 4B).

About Riverside Resources Inc.

Riverside is a well-funded exploration company driven by value generation and discovery. The Company has a solid balance sheet with no debt and fewer than 95M shares outstanding with a strong portfolio of gold-silver and copper assets and royalties in North America. Riverside has extensive experience and knowledge operating in Mexico and Canada and leverages its large database to generate a portfolio of prospective mineral properties. Riverside has properties available for option, with information available on the Company’s website at www.rivres.com.
